server.description: Screen agent, DAO, and reputation designs against 32 named failure modes with checkable conditions
server.title: AFMR: Agent Failure Mode Registry, and the Kaal Corpus claim layer

author.affiliation: University of St. Thomas School of Law, Minneapolis
author.name: Wulf A. Kaal

corpus.count_note: The scholarly roster is pinned at 140. The 5,655-claim layer currently covers 138 hash-backed works. Two roster records are metadata-only until their source PDFs and claims are ingested.
corpus.source_taxonomy_note: The 57 families are a broader corpus taxonomy. They are not the AFMR standard family count. AFMR 1.0 refines the agent-relevant material into 32 named families.

distribution.note: Both URLs serve the same bytes. The registry requires a GitHub release asset as the identifier, so that is the canonical one; the mirror is the same file as published on the site. Hash either and compare.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.license: Attribution required. Read, index, quote and cite with attribution to the claim's canonical URL.

verification.quote_guarantee: every supporting quote is an exact contiguous substring of its source text; extraction rejected any claim whose quote did not match, and both the compiler and an independent verifier report zero failures
verification.source_pdf_hash: each record names the sha256 of the PDF the quote was extracted from; hashing that file checks the claim against its evidence rather than against this index
verification.summary: Retrieval here is checkable rather than asserted. Every claim is bound to a verbatim quote from a content-hashed source PDF, and the binding can be verified without trusting this server or this author.

packageArguments.description: Run the MCP server over stdio.

packageArguments.description: Project root this server serves. Required, and resolved once at startup: one process serves exactly one repository, so every tool call reads and writes that project's task store. Point it at your own repo.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.authentication: None. Local-first: no login is required and no API key is needed.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.longDescription: Task management for AI coding agents over MCP and CLI. Agents claim sequenced tasks, implement, and submit for review; humans get a local-first kanban board. UI annotation files tickets with selector, file and line; verification gates the review.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.releaseNote: This manifest is pinned to 0.26.0, the published version of @vibeflow-tools/cli. Verified against the installed package, not the repository: an MCP `tools/list` handshake against `@vibeflow-tools/cli@0.26.0` returns 12 tools, and those names match `packages/cli/src/mcp/manifest.ts` exactly. The `tools` count here therefore matches the README's tool table.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.transport: stdio, one process per project. An HTTP transport also exists (vibeflow serve, MCP at /api/mcp) but it is a local loopback server, not a public endpoint, so this manifest declares no remotes.

server.name: io.github.zz-plant/ambit
server.description: Capability graph of your agent stack: what it can do, what to set up next, what breaks.

packageArguments.description: Run the MCP server over stdio instead of the terminal CLI

consumes.effect: A foreign discrepancy about a capability this graph knows is recorded as evidence attributed to the sending environment. It does not move a lifecycle: a peer reporting a capability broken does not narrow a grant here, only where the check actually failed.
consumes.from: another Ambit environment, which runs the same tech tree and so names capabilities identically. A source whose system is ambit must name its instance, and cannot name this one.
consumes.how: ambit delegation ingest <file>, or a source declared with `ambit delegation source add` and read on every full verification run

org.ethotechnics.revisable-delegation.enforced: An unattended grant whose hard prerequisite is failing returns CONFIRM at every decision, whether or not any record has been written.

notEmitted.why: Ambit holds the capability and authorization steps. Its environment adapter is simulated, so an action record from here would attest to a fixture.

org.ethotechnics.revisable-delegation.note: Level 2 for a stream from a graph nobody has objected in. Every record declares standing, so a stream containing an objection and its answer measures at Level 3.
org.ethotechnics.revisable-delegation.upstream: derived at runtime from declared sources; see `ambit delegation` output. Empty until a person declares one.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.overview:
Find your next B2B customers. Know why they fit.

Describe the companies you want to reach. Leadbase researches matching businesses and relevant decision-makers, then saves the results with sources in an editable sheet. Start with 200 free credits in a new workspace and test your own target market.

Qualify companies by the criteria that matter to your offer: services, region and publicly evidenced business signals. Research DACH SMEs and German craft businesses alongside other target markets.

Turn existing accounts into a more useful prospect list. Enrich selected rows or entire columns, research relevant professional contacts and check available contact details. Review the evidence behind returned information before choosing your next step.

Keep control of the result. Follow progress, edit your sheet, filter the list and export the data. Continue the same research instead of rebuilding the list each time.

Use Leadbase with ChatGPT, Claude, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other compatible MCP clients. Connect your workspace and ask for a small list in your own target market. Research uses workspace credits.

The endpoint must answer to the same model name as NOETIVE_MODEL and return NOETIVE_DIMENSIONS values. Plain http is accepted only for a loopback address. Inside a container 127.0.0.1 is the container itself; use host.docker.internal.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.description:
CartRelay — Your agent’s favourite marketplace. Discover product options through one interface across currently approved Awin programmes and transient Shopify Global Catalog queries. Native MCP retains five tools and its legacy Canada/CAD and US/USD input surface; explicit global market input is REST-only Shopify and is not a claim of stock or shipping coverage.

Inspect native tool metadata before connecting. Product and commerce operations still require valid authentication. Preserve exact variants, merchant attribution, source-native prices and unknown availability; retailer confirms final cost and stock. CartRelay prepares expiring review intents, and retailer handoff requires independent shopper approval and fresh selection checks. CartRelay does not buy, reserve stock or process payment.

The private catalogue is not a bulk export or public mirror. Internal test datasets are not publicly available. Installing an integration or seeing this listing is not proof of agent adoption, completed purchases or guaranteed current offers.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.longDescription: Ranked (ranked.ng) is a directory of Nigerian businesses. This server exposes nine read-only tools over it. Three read the production database: the ordered ranking for a category in a Nigerian city, served only where the base page is published; one place page with its rank on its primary published facet and any regulator register matches; and the indexable hub URLs on ranked.ng with counts. Six read committed files with no database: search across the file-backed dataset, whether a name appears on the CBN, SEC, NAICOM, NCC or PenCom register as accessed on a dated snapshot, a regulator's register in the regulator's own order, whether someone in Nigeria can pay for a named product (naira pricing, card acceptance, local rails, geo-restriction), the same rubric for two to five products side by side, and a stats tool reporting what the server holds and each register's access date. Every answer carries a canonical ranked.ng URL and an 'as accessed on' date. A register match is what that regulator's register listed on the access date, not a licence finding by Ranked. The server never writes, takes no payment, and returns no personal contact data.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.title: Ranked

github.readme:
# taxapp.nz

Ask your AI app about your [Tax App](https://taxapp.nz) records in plain words: income, expenses, rental properties and New Zealand tax. Where your organisation allows it, it can add and change records too.

## Sign-in required

Every request needs you to sign in to Tax App. Your AI app opens the Tax App sign-in page when you connect; there is no key or password to copy into it.

## What you can ask

- "What is my estimated tax for this year?"
- "Which expenses did I record for the rental in March?"
- "Which bank transactions still need sorting?"
- "Add a $120 plumber bill for 12 Smith Street."
- "The rent at 12 Smith Street goes up to $680 a week from 1 June."
- "Change last week's commission payment to $1,250."

The figures come straight from your records. The answer is written by the AI, so check anything that matters in the app.

## Before you connect

1. You need a Tax App account. [Sign up free](https://app.taxapp.nz/signup).
2. An owner of your organisation turns AI connectors on in **Settings > AI connectors**, or while connecting, and chooses **Read only** or **Read, add and change records**.
3. Add the server in your AI app and sign in to Tax App when asked. [Steps for each AI app](https://taxapp.nz/guides/ai-assistants/).

## What it can do

| Area | Read | Add and change |
|------|------|----------------|
| Tax year | overview, tax summary, profit and loss | |
| Income | history, list, one record | commission, rent or tenant reimbursement |
| Expenses | list, one record, expense accounts | expenses, expense accounts |
| Contacts | list, contact types | contacts, PAYE salary, ACC classifications, contact types |
| Rental properties | list with tenancies, rental report | properties, tenancies |
| Savings | savings plan | savings plan |
| Scheduled reports | list, reports that can be scheduled (owners) | schedules (owners), send one now |
| Choices | record types and IRD return lines, in your own words | |
| Bank | bank inbox, reconciliation status | |

Adding and changing is off unless an owner chooses **Read, add and change records**, and never goes beyond your own role. The AI app sends only what you tell it, such as dates, amounts and who paid: Tax App works out GST, KiwiSaver, ACC levy, tax and every total itself, exactly as it does on its own forms. When a detail is unclear, such as which contact, property or expense account you mean, the AI app shows you the closest matches and asks.

## What it cannot do

- Delete anything
- Reconcile bank statements or change a match
- Change organisation settings or members
- See anything your own role cannot, or an organisation you did not tick
- File a return with Inland Revenue

## Keeping it safe

- It signs in as you and never sees your password.
- Every change it makes is in the organisation's audit trail, marked as made through the AI connector.
- Owners see every AI connector under **Settings > AI connectors** and can remove any of them; switching AI connectors off ends them all.
- Changing your password ends every AI connector you made.
- What you share goes to the company behind your AI app, under its own terms, and may be kept outside New Zealand. Your records in Tax App stay where they are.
- Tax, ACC and KiwiSaver figures are indicative workings from IRD rates, not an IRD assessment.

## For app developers

- Authentication: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE (S256). A request without a valid sign-in gets HTTP 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge.
- Authorization server: `https://api.taxapp.nz` (dynamic client registration and client ID metadata documents)
- Protected resource metadata: `https://mcp.taxapp.nz/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`
- Scope: `taxapp`. No API key, header or environment variable to configure.

## More

- [Full guide](https://taxapp.nz/guides/ai-assistants/)
- [Privacy policy](https://taxapp.nz/privacy/)
- Help: support@taxapp.nz

packageArguments.description: The CLI command group that hosts the Model Context Protocol surface.
Serve the belief store over stdio. Read-only by default: the read tools are always registered, and the write tools are added only for stores explicitly listed in `mcp.write.enabled_stores`.

environmentVariables.description: Anthropic API key. Required for the tools that call a model — `query` composes a cited natural-language answer, and the semantic half of `lint` reasons over claim pairs. The accessors that only read the store (`particle_show`, `particles_list`, `subjects_*`, `events_*`, `graph_view`, `quality_report`) work without it.
environmentVariables.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

environmentVariables.description: SQLAlchemy URL of the belief store to serve, used as given, so write a SQLite path absolute: a relative one opens against the directory the server starts in. Without it, and without PARTICLES_CONFIG, the server serves the store `~/.particles/config.yaml` names (a relative path there is read under `~/.particles/`), or `~/.particles/particles.db` when that file names none, never a store in the directory it starts in.
environmentVariables.name: DATABASE_URL

environmentVariables.description: Path to the config file holding the rest of the server's settings: additional stores, model selection per purpose, and the `mcp.write.enabled_stores` allowlist that turns the write tools on. This is the supported way to give the server settings. Without it the server reads `~/.particles/config.yaml`, never a `config.yaml` in the directory it starts in. Give it as an absolute path: a relative one is refused. When you set it, also set `DATABASE_URL` to an absolute path or name one as `storage.database_url` in the file: a server started with a config file refuses a store path relative to its working directory, and refuses to start while any store under `storage.stores` has one.
environmentVariables.name: PARTICLES_CONFIG

toolSurface.writeGate: mcp.write.enabled_stores is empty by default; a store must be named there before any write tool is registered.

pipeline.description: Apply an ordered pipeline of image ops in a single paid call: one payment, one output. Price is the sum of the included ops’ prices — call without payment to get a 402 quote. Input: source (image URL), steps (ordered [{op, params}], e.g. [{"op":"remove_background"},{"op":"resize","params":{"width":800}}]). Call service_info for the available ops and their per-op prices. Output: the processed image as a short-lived signed URL.
pipeline.name: process
pipeline.pricing: dynamic: sum of the included ops’ prices

tools.description: Remove an image's background, isolating the subject (BiRefNet AI segmentation). $0.02 per call. Input: an image via source URL. Params: background (optional fill color for the removed area, e.g. 'white'; omit for a transparent cutout — use a PNG/WebP output to keep transparency). Output: the cut-out image as a short-lived signed URL.
tools.name: remove_background

tools.description: Upscale an image with AI super-resolution (ESRGAN) for sharper enlargement. $0.02 per call. Input: an image via source URL. Params: width and/or height (target pixels; at least one required). Output: the enlarged image as a short-lived signed URL.
tools.name: upscale

tools.description: Resize or crop an image to an exact width/height. $0.005 per call. Input: an image via source URL. Params: width, height (pixels); fit (scale-down|contain|pad|squeeze|cover|crop); gravity (auto|face|left|right|top|bottom|center|entropy — focal point for cover/crop, use 'face' to keep faces); background (fill color for 'pad', e.g. 'white' or 'rgba(0,0,0,0)' for transparent). At least one of width/height is required. Output: the transformed image as a short-lived signed URL.
tools.name: resize

tools.description: Convert format and/or compress an image. $0.005 per call. Input: an image via source URL. Params: format (webp|avif|jpeg|png|gif); quality (1-100, default 85 — lower is smaller). At least one of format/quality is required. Output: the optimized image as a short-lived signed URL.
tools.name: optimize

se.bizindex.beskrivning_sv: Bizindex är ett öppet index över svenska aktiebolag. Tre verktyg som bara läser: registeruppgifter ur Bolagsverkets och SCB:s register, vilken webbplats som är kopplad till bolaget och belägget för kopplingen, vilka tjänster startsidan nämner, en spårningskontroll av startsidan och, för elektriker och takläggare, registrering hos Elsäkerhetsverket. Varje svar har källor och datum. Ingen nyckel och ingen inloggning. Synlighetspoängen ingår inte. Drivs av Snabba Pucks AB, som också säljer synlighetstjänster. Ingen kan betala för en bättre plats.
se.bizindex.description_en: Bizindex is an open index of Swedish limited companies (aktiebolag). Three read-only tools return registry data from Bolagsverket and Statistics Sweden (SCB), which website is linked to the company and the evidence for the link, which services the homepage mentions, a check of whether the homepage tracks visitors before consent and, for electricians and roofers, registration with the Swedish Electrical Safety Authority. Every answer has sources and dates. No key and no login. The visibility score is not included. Run by Snabba Pucks AB, which also sells visibility services. Nobody can pay for a better position.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.longDescription:
SECONDED is the oracle for agents. Before your agent acts, it checks the real cost, the real contract and the real risk, read live and confirmed by two rival AIs, one from OpenAI and one from Anthropic. If they don't agree, you don't pay. Every answer comes with a signed receipt.

8 checks: Trade Check ($0.25 small, $1.50 medium); Stock Token Check ($0.25 small); Token Check ($0.25 small); Agent Registry Check ($0.25 small); Counterparty Address Check ($0.25 small); Cross-Chain Compare ($0.25 small); Scam Check ($0.25 small, $1.50 medium, $2.50 large); Lending Check ($0.50 small). Payment networks: Base USDC (eip155:8453); Arc USDC (eip155:5042); Robinhood Chain USDG (eip155:4663). Base mainnet is the default; other networks require explicit selection. Payments use POST /v1/x402/checks; /v1/checks is operator rollback only until all three mainnet canaries pass. New wallets: $2.50 per check, $25/day. Chat may only tighten or freeze; raising limits, unfreezing and switching wallets require the owner terminal. Legacy nil or above-$25/day policies freeze pending owner review. Automatic private-file fallback is UNENCRYPTED; fund a dedicated wallet with only a few dollars. Native binaries have no Apple notarization or Windows Authenticode; verify the SSH-signed SHA-256 manifest.
